technical_and_design_decisions: Define a common Admin SPI and module-registry abstraction with getStatus, listModules, and status-by-module-key operations.
Keep Receptor and Cloud Controller implementations behind the same SPI, selected through Spring profiles and conditional bean configuration.
Use existing Cloud Foundry and Receptor client libraries where available rather than implementing protocol clients from scratch.
Represent module identity with ModuleDescriptor and ModuleDescriptor.Key, and use the descriptor as the stable lookup key across implementations.
Implement Eureka integration using standard Eureka client registration and metadata facilities.
Use a dedicated module-name metadata field for searching, while retaining spring.application.name as the default application identity.
Treat Eureka registration and metadata as the source used by the module registry for discovery and current-state lookup.
Add unit tests for registry and adapter behavior, plus integration tests using mocks or in-memory test doubles for Receptor, Cloud Controller, and Eureka.
Preserve backward compatibility for existing Spring XD administrative commands and default deployment behavior.
assumptions: The estimate covers implementation, automated tests, local verification, and developer documentation, but not production deployment or operational rollout.
The existing Spring XD codebase, Admin SPI types, ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus, deployment model, and build infrastructure are available and buildable.
Required Java, Spring, Cloud Foundry, Receptor, and Eureka client dependencies either already exist or can be added without major upstream changes.
Receptor and Cloud Controller expose sufficient APIs to retrieve module status, list deployed modules, and obtain health-related information.
The existing project already has configuration and profile conventions that can be extended for java -jar admin, cf push admin, and ltc create admin scenarios.
Eureka server infrastructure is external to this increment; only client registration, metadata publication, lookup, and test support are included.
No major migration of existing persisted module data or production Eureka data is required.
One developer performs the work sequentially, with normal code review represented by self-review and automated validation rather than separate staffing.
Unspecified error handling, retry, timeout, authentication, and partial-failure behavior will follow existing project conventions.
The specification does not define detailed acceptance criteria, so the estimate assumes one implementation path and a normal level of edge-case handling.

activities.activity_description: Inspect existing Admin SPI, deployment adapters, module descriptors, profile configuration, Eureka integration points, build layout, and test conventions; produce the implementation design and compatibility plan.

activities.activity_name: Common SPI repository and package organization
activities.activity_description: Create or relocate the permanent common location for SPI implementations, update module dependencies and package references, and ensure the common repository structure builds cleanly.
Implement the module registry interfaces and domain integration needed to list modules, retrieve a module status, retrieve statuses by module key, and support test doubles for registry providers.
Implement the Receptor-backed Admin SPI adapter, including module discovery, status and health mapping, error handling, descriptor conversion, and integration with the module registry.
Implement the Cloud Controller-backed Admin SPI adapter, including deployed-module listing, status and health mapping, descriptor conversion, client interaction, and failure handling.

Add and validate Spring profile and conditional-bean configuration so the appropriate Receptor or Cloud Controller implementation is selected automatically for the supported admin execution and deployment modes.
Add module startup registration with Eureka, including registration lifecycle handling, module identity mapping, deregistration behavior where supported, and configuration of registration properties.
Publish module metadata to Eureka, support an explicit module-name attribute in addition to spring.application.name, and implement registry lookup and filtering by module name and current state.

Create tests for registry contracts, both SPI adapters, profile selection, Eureka registration and metadata, module-name search, status mapping, error cases, and end-to-end administrative queries using mocks or test doubles.

Update build and dependency configuration, document profiles and configuration properties, run focused and full test suites, perform compatibility checks, and resolve integration defects found during verification.
Perform self-review, inspect logging and failure behavior, verify backward compatibility and packaging for supported launch modes, clean up APIs, and prepare the increment for handoff.
